title: Surgical PR routing + rewrite checklist (scratchpad)
body:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for tackling the PR that changes the request routing stack (router/ref klient patch). Goal is a minimal, surgical rewrite to:
- make route matching deterministic for feature-flagged traffic
- add a lightweight fallback chain for overloaded pools
- ensure observability hooks are fired per-route (cost + latency breakdown)

High-level constraints / guardrails:
- Keep public API identical (no client-facing config change) — we only change internal control-plane routing behavior.
- Rollout must support canary (10%) -> 50% -> 100% with instant rollback.
- No synchronous blocking on cache warm-ups during request path.
- Must not regress tail latency on existing synthetic suite (<1% regression).

Quick hypothesis to validate:
- Current matching algorithm loops a lot for multi-criteria routes, causing 2–3x CPU on ab_tested traffic. A trie-based index keyed by (model, region, tier) should reduce comparisons.
- Adding a compact route fingerprint to request headers will speed up routing in hot path.

Checklist for reviewers (what I want feedback on) — prioritize left-to-right in PR description:
- [ ] correctness: unit tests for exact-match, prefix-match, and wildcard combos (see test cases below).
- [ ] performance: microbench harness results included (before/after median + p95).
- [ ] deterministic ordering: ensure stable sort on route priority and creation timestamp.
- [ ] fallback behavior: simulate pool OOM/overload and confirm fallback candidate picked within 2ms.
- [ ] observability: ensure route_id + policy_id emitted as span tags and in request logs.
- [ ] holiday edge cases: rules with missing region should default to global not error.
- [ ] documentation: short section in serving-runtime/README about routing invariants.

Test cases to include in unit/integration suite (skeleton):
- exact_match_basic: route A (model=v1) should match request model=v1, reject model=v2.
- prefix_and_wildcard: prefix routes and wildcard should prefer exact then prefix then wildcard.
- feature_flag_override: if request has header x-ff-canary=on pick canary route.
- simultaneous_pool_failure: two pools fail, fallback picks third with spare capacity.
- ordering_stability: create routes in different orders then query same key -> same result.

Benchmarks to run (local harness):
- local_routing_micro: 10M lookups, compare ns/lookup before/after. Capture median/p95/p99.
- integration_loadtest: 10k qps for 60s against dev env, with KV-cache warm/unwarm cycles. Capture tail-latency and cpu.

Refactor ideas (non-blocking for this PR, follow-up):
- pull out RouteIndex into an interface with two implementations (trie vs linear) behind a feature flag. Easier rollback.
- introduce a small Bloom filter per-route to quickly exclude impossible requests (cheap memory, reduces comparisons).
- move heavy matching logic to background precomputation step during route updates; keep lookup hot path minimal.

Risk matrix / rollback plan:
- Risk: subtle mismatch in prefix semantics -> Bad route selection for small subset. Mitigation: run traffic shadowing for 24h before canary, add metric for 'route-change-rate' per route.
- Risk: increased GC from new data structure. Mitigation: run heap profiles, set rate-limited adult gen tuning.
- Rollback: revert flag for new routing impl OR toggle route-index feature flag to old implementation; document exact flag names and expected behavior in PR.

Open questions for reviewers (explicit asks in PR):
- Do we prefer a single route_id per route or composite (route_set_id + ordinal)? Composite simplifies rollouts but costs storage in logs.
- Is the header-fingerprinting acceptable from a security/data-class standpoint? (I think yes — low entropy derived from non-PII fields)
- Should routing metrics be dimensioned by tenant_id or aggregated at cluster level to avoid too many metric series?

Follow-ups / TODOs (post-merge):
- [ ] Add canary orchestration docs to product/hosted-api runbook.
- [ ] Add light e2e that asserts observability tags arrive in tracing pipeline.
- [ ] Automate benchmark from CI -> store baselines in S3.
- [ ] Add a small fuzzer for route matching combinations (order matters).

Notes to self (things I hit while coding) — chronological:
- had to convert route.matchers from slice->map for faster deletes; watch for nil map panics.
- found global variable routeCache causing flakiness in tests; moved to test-scoped store.
- minor PR ergonomics: keep commits small and self-contained; first commit is purely tests + fixtures, second is implementation, third is perf tweak.

Slack / links to ping on approval:
- #serving-runtime for smoke/bench signoff
- pings: @eli, @maya for perf review, @luca for SRE worries

Quick local commands I used / recommend for reviewers to reproduce perf numbers:
- go test ./routing -bench=BenchmarkRouteLookup -run=^$ -benchmem -count=3
- ./bin/loadtest --qps=5000 --dur=60 --target http://dev-routing:8080/route

Small code snippet (pseudo) for safe lookup pattern to avoid allocations:
- do not allocate strings per-request, use []byte slices and compare with bytes.Equal
- caching: fingerprint := twentyBitHash(req.model, req.region, req.tier)
- idx.Get(fingerprint) -> candidate list -> verify in order

Last-minute: make sure PR description contains a short TL;DR + list of commits and how reviewers should step through them. Keep this doc as the mental checklist while addressing comments.

Misc brain-dump (one-liners):
- "If it can't be tested deterministically, don't ship it."
- prefer small feature flags over large runtime switches.
- instrument early: emit a debug metric for 'routing_candidates_examined' and sample it to logs for hot complaints.

End of scratchpad.

(If I close this and come back later, add a short changelog at top and mark completed checkboxes.)
